newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus to deregulate rates by early 1998.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus to deregulate rates by early 1998.

text.p: Cyprus will deregulate its interest rates and free capital flows by the end of 1997 or in early 1998, the island's finance minister said on Thursday.

Finance Minister Christodoulos Christodoulou told Reuters the government would discuss the move with interested parties before submitting legislation abolishing the ceiling which has been in force since 1944. It is currently set at nine percent.
"No bill shall be forwarded to the House before all interested parties have been contacted and before a dialogue," he said, after delivering his annual budget speech to parliament.
But he added: "The whole system will be liberalised before the start of entry negotiations which means either the end of 1997 or the very beginning of 1998."
The government sees deregulation of rates and the free movement of capital as a key move it will have to take before it starts entry negotiations with the European Union.
Negotiations are due to start six months after the end of an EU intergovernmental conference.
Cooperative societies oppose deregulation along with the communist Akel, the second largest party with 19 deputies in the 56-member House of Representatives.
They believe the move could drive rates up with serious consequences for thousands of people with often large loans.
"I strongly believe the Cyprus market is not ready to accept the deregulation of rates," said Kikis Kazamias, an Akel deputy.
He accused the government of "double talk".

"The minister repeated today that a political decision has been taken to liberalise interest rates...other government officials have said there has not been a decision to liberalise this sector. There is a contradiction."
